sermon.title: A Fourth, and Much Overlooked, Reason Sheep Go Astray
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches the fourth and most overlooked reason sheep go astray: treacherous sheep who befriend the weak and wounded to push them into error. He recounts harm from twisted teaching in his ministry and failed end-time predictions, then lists what these sheep lack: doing good, fellowship, obeying those who rule, provoking to love and good works, and continuing in the apostles’ doctrine. Jesus is able to overcome it all.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Points to check: “koinonia” called a Hebrew word in the captions (it is Greek; corrected in transcript); Peter’s Pentecost sermon attributed to “Paul” and “four thousand” saved (Acts 2:41 says about 3,000); Chuck Smith 1981 prediction, William Branham 1977, Hal Lindsey 1988 and moon-dust figures as spoken. Sensitive content kept as spoken: self-harm and suicides of young men over twisted teaching (private, unnamed); named ministers Doug Clark, Pat Robertson, Chuck Smith, William Branham, Hal Lindsey, Kenneth Hagin, Jerry Falwell; elders “most worthless people”; man with 17 children on welfare; redneck men demanding submission; homosexuality and divorce.

chunks.section_question: What were the first three reasons sheep go astray?
chunks.short_answer: Each going his own way (Isaiah 53), the “whoevers” who cause little ones and young believers to sin, and the delegated shepherds who scatter the flock. The fourth is the most overlooked and treacherous: befriending someone to harm them—people who show up when you are sick or disagree with the church and believe sin is okay.

faqs.question: What is the fourth reason sheep go astray?
faqs.answer: Treacherous sheep who befriend young believers to harm them.

faqs.question: When is division justified?
faqs.answer: Only when Jesus or morality is distorted.

faqs.question: Whom do the butting sheep target?
faqs.answer: The weak and wounded—young believers and children.

faqs.question: What does the Holy Spirit do?
faqs.answer: He convicts of sin and teaches us.

faqs.question: What went wrong in those home Bible studies?
faqs.answer: People twisted Scripture and caused tremendous harm.

faqs.question: Can submission be forced?
faqs.answer: No—you choose to submit; God gives a choice.

faqs.question: Where does church authority come from?
Did Jesus only speak of peace?
faqs.answer: No—he said he came to bring a sword.
